source.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)

scope: All 74 canonical requirements representing 72 AI RMF 1.0 Core subcategories; source meaning/scope and context already primary-text reviewed.
class_comparison_scope: All 76 selectable neutral class invariants, using their definitions and exclusions to distinguish institutional/assessment duties from operational mechanisms.

entries.requirement_summary: Provide policies and practices to collect, consider, prioritize and integrate feedback from outside the development or deployment team about potential individual and societal impacts related to AI risks.
entries.rationale: External stakeholder impact feedback is participatory risk governance; no current FC directly represents systematic participation and prioritisation.

entries.requirement_summary: Follow and document processes for tracking, responding to and recovering from incidents and errors.
entries.rationale: Incident/error tracking/response/recovery and communication are relevant to event capture and governance delivery; they do not specify all material-event records or capable destinations/disposition tracking.

candidate_class_relationships.invariant: Every materially consequential action, state change, control decision, handoff, and failure must create and retain an evidence record at or near occurrence, with content and duration proportionate to oversight, incident response, and reconstruction needs.
candidate_class_relationships.supported_component: Incident/error tracking/response/recovery and communication are relevant to event capture and governance delivery; they do not specify all material-event records or capable destinations/disposition tracking.
scope_qualifications: Voluntary organisational application of AI RMF Core; not binding law.
No occurrence applicability or finding follows from this analytical correspondence.

candidate_class_relationships.invariant: A material governance signal must carry an accountable owner, capable destination, status, response expectation, and escalation route, and remain tracked until it produces the required effect or receives an authorised disposition. Emission, acknowledgement, or storage at an incapable endpoint is not completion.
candidate_class_relationships.supported_component: Incident/error tracking/response/recovery and communication are relevant to event capture and governance delivery; they do not specify all material-event records or capable destinations/disposition tracking.
scope_qualifications: Voluntary organisational application of AI RMF Core; not binding law.
No occurrence applicability or finding follows from this analytical correspondence.

entries.requirement_summary: Organizational risk tolerances are determined and documented.
entries.rationale: Documented organisational risk tolerance is policy input; do not equate it with authority to override independent safety/ecological constraints.

entries.requirement_summary: Develop, plan and document responses to high-priority AI risks identified in MAP; response options may include mitigation, transfer, avoidance or acceptance.
entries.rationale: Plans for high-priority risk responses include mitigation/transfer/avoidance/acceptance options; no particular activation/effect/safe-exit obligation follows solely from those alternatives.

entries.requirement_summary: Monitor pre-trained models used for development as part of regular AI system monitoring and maintenance.
entries.rationale: Pre-trained-model monitoring/maintenance supports current-state awareness, but does not expressly invalidate prior verification after material dependency changes or guarantee all-route coverage.

candidate_class_relationships.invariant: A prior verification may support a later claim only while its applicability to the current time, target, state, version, environment, dependencies, and scope remains established. Otherwise it is historical evidence and the current claim must be revalidated or marked unresolved.
candidate_class_relationships.supported_component: Pre-trained-model monitoring/maintenance supports current-state awareness, but does not expressly invalidate prior verification after material dependency changes or guarantee all-route coverage.
scope_qualifications: Voluntary organisational application of AI RMF Core; not binding law.
No occurrence applicability or finding follows from this analytical correspondence.

candidate_class_relationships.invariant: Required monitoring coverage must be preserved across agents, subagents, tools, services, environments, configurations, routes, and transitions. A coverage-changing path must be validated before use and may proceed only under the required monitor or an authorised equivalent.
candidate_class_relationships.supported_component: Pre-trained-model monitoring/maintenance supports current-state awareness, but does not expressly invalidate prior verification after material dependency changes or guarantee all-route coverage.
scope_qualifications: Voluntary organisational application of AI RMF Core; not binding law.
No occurrence applicability or finding follows from this analytical correspondence.

entries.requirement_summary: The appropriateness of metrics and effectiveness of controls are regularly assessed and updated, including errors and impacts on affected communities.
entries.rationale: Regular control-effectiveness assessment distinguishes realised protective capability from mere nominal control presence. FC-000083 additionally requires a valid operative control, hazard-specific timeliness, proportionality and sufficiency; this is supporting evaluation, not full equivalence.

candidate_class_relationships.invariant: When a protective control validly becomes operative, its effect must be timely, proportionate, and sufficient for the hazard and protection context it governs. Detection, warning, labelling, refusal language, escalation signalling, or other nominal activation is not by itself sufficient where the required protective effect is not achieved and the governed harmful state is delivered, continues, or remains inadequately contained. Required protective sufficiency may increase where evidenced developmental vulnerability, capacity limitation, temporary or situational consent impairment, acute distress, cognitive asymmetry, or comparable protection conditions materially affect the risk, but disability or neurodivergence alone must not be treated as incapacity.
candidate_class_relationships.supported_component: Regular control-effectiveness assessment distinguishes realised protective capability from mere nominal control presence. FC-000083 additionally requires a valid operative control, hazard-specific timeliness, proportionality and sufficiency; this is supporting evaluation, not full equivalence.
scope_qualifications: Voluntary organisational application of AI RMF Core; not binding law.
No occurrence applicability or finding follows from this analytical correspondence.

entries.requirement_summary: Organizational teams document and communicate AI-system risks and potential impacts.
entries.rationale: AI-risk documentation and wider communication support information flow; accountable capable destinations, correlation, response expectation and disposition are not specified.

Individual capture is insufficient where operationally disconnected signals prevent recognition of the material state.

entries.requirement_summary: Organizations applying the NIST AI RMF should ensure that their evaluations of AI systems involving human subjects are representative of the population relevant to those evaluations.
entries.rationale: Relevant-population representativeness supports the fitness/source-quality component of evaluation assurance. It does not establish a consequential reliance threshold or universal demographic quotas.

candidate_class_relationships.invariant: Before an epistemic artefact is promoted, accepted, or used in a materially consequential decision, its assurance posture must meet the downstream reliance threshold, calibrated to source quality, traceability, independence, uncertainty, temporal fitness, and error consequences. Lower-assurance material must remain provisional.
candidate_class_relationships.supported_component: Relevant-population representativeness supports the fitness/source-quality component of evaluation assurance. It does not establish a consequential reliance threshold or universal demographic quotas.
scope_qualifications: Voluntary organisational application of AI RMF Core; not binding law.
No occurrence applicability or finding follows from this analytical correspondence.

entries.requirement_summary: AI-system security and resilience are evaluated and documented.
entries.rationale: Security/resilience evaluation is technical assurance. No specific authority, recovery or adversarial-evidence mechanism is supplied by this broad security proposition.

entries.requirement_summary: Document AI system knowledge limits and how outputs may be used and overseen by humans, with sufficient information to assist relevant AI actors in decisions and subsequent actions.
entries.rationale: Documenting knowledge limits and permissible output use/human oversight supplies bounded assurance information for responsible reliance. It does not establish FC-000062’s consequential decision threshold or that assurance actually meets it.

entries.requirement_summary: Integrate measurable continual-improvement activities into AI system updates, including regular engagement with interested parties and relevant AI actors.
entries.rationale: Continual improvement and engagement are institutional learning practices; no single current operational invariant materially represents this programme duty.

entries.requirement_summary: Organizations applying the NIST AI RMF should ensure that their evaluations of AI systems involving human subjects meet requirements applicable to those evaluations, including protection of human subjects.
entries.rationale: Human-subject protection/applicable evaluation requirements are research-protection governance. Generic participant authority classes do not exhaust these protections; no specific consent, authority or data-use duty is inferred.

entries.requirement_summary: Provide, follow and document approaches for mapping AI technology and legal risks of system components, including third-party data or software, and document risks of infringing third-party intellectual property or other rights.
entries.rationale: Component technology/legal/IP risk mapping helps identify rights risks; it does not itself require authority revalidation for a particular secondary use or contribution-return arrangement.

candidate_class_relationships.invariant: Before data or an identifiable contribution is used for a materially different secondary purpose, the system, provider, deployer, or governance process must independently establish a sufficient authority or governance basis for the secondary purpose, affected data or contribution, relevant target or recipient, scope, persistence, and downstream effect. Prior participation, prior processing, routing, fusion, public availability, silence, or absence of objection must not establish that basis. Where custody, persistence, sharing, propagation, or downstream consequence materially changes, the applicable authority and rights state must be revalidated and remain legible and auditable.
candidate_class_relationships.supported_component: Component technology/legal/IP risk mapping helps identify rights risks; it does not itself require authority revalidation for a particular secondary use or contribution-return arrangement.
scope_qualifications: Voluntary organisational application of AI RMF Core; not binding law.
No occurrence applicability or finding follows from this analytical correspondence.

Safety metrics reflect reliability, robustness, real-time monitoring and failure response times.
entries.rationale: Safety evaluation, residual risk tolerance, fail-safe capability and metrics supply safety assurance context. They do not by themselves define a valid triggered control’s required effect or exhaustion-based safe-exit condition.

candidate_class_relationships.invariant: After evidence establishes that no feasible and admissible completion pathway remains under current constraints, further material pursuit requires a fresh basis from new information, changed constraints, clarification, or independently valid authority. Otherwise the system must enter a bounded safe-exit state. Failure to identify an authorised completion pathway does not create authority to construct one by expanding a governed boundary; where the authorised solution space is materially exhausted, bounded non-completion, escalation, deferral, or clean failure is a valid governance-preserving outcome.
